doc.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Recording Hair, the band, 'Happy Feet' and Michael Butler
summary: The show is recorded and sells about 80 million records; Lewis names the band, voices the music, writes 'Happy Feet', and tells of backer Michael Butler and the five-year run.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: all my bass lines. So then it comes time to record this Broadway show. So we recorded it. And the thing was a hit.
Yeah. I think in about two years they sold about 80 million records.
Your stamp was all over that thing.

Oh, yeah, yeah. I spent a lot of time trying to get the sound. Like they had a Zane Paul, and Don Leight. Zane Paul, he played bass clarinet and tenor and alto. Don Leight trumpet. Eddy Williams trumpet. And Neal Tate piano, Idris Muhammed on drums, and Charlie Brown acoustic guitar and let’s see who else did we have? Oh, Alan Fontaine, he played guitar, electric guitar. So now what I did, I said now I’ve got to voice this stuff to make it sound different from anything. Because the show is different from anything you ever heard of. It looked like it wasn’t anything. I figured it’d last about two weeks. So we got the thing together and did it. Then the critics came in and they listened, and they watched the show, and they liked it so well, man, doggone it was a hit. All right now. The thing was a hit and we had to already record the music. But I wasn’t satisfied with the sound. So I took it and polished it up. So Galt said, “look, I got to do another show,” and they said, “you just take care of the music part, you know, and hold the band together.” So I changed the whole style of the band. Not really, the music was the same except I updated it a little bit. And the kids went crazy on the floor man, oh, they were so glad to do the show. But they had in the opening of the show where they’d sit there and talk on the floor. And so I said well they need something in this act. So I created a tune called “Happy Feet.” And they played it very softly. You’ve got to really listen to hear it you know, but it was just the rhythm section you know, two guitars, electric bass and piano. We’d play that thing man, and it was almost like a jazz tune in parts you know. So boy we played that thing and the people in the audience, you could see them moving to the music you know. All right, but we never really put it in the show you know. I just wanted to fill it there. And when we got ready to close, this is what got me. We got in there one day, and Michael Butler, he was the guy that had all the money. And I think he said he had three hundred million dollars, and when he came to back the show you know, his father had some money he inherited. And so he was a young guy. He didn’t know what to do with it, so he said well I’ll do this. He used to give us big parties. We’d ride up and down Fifth Avenue in those double decker things and it was nice. The Four Seasons — we’d go to the Four Seasons and all this. So Michael one night, after about, let’s see we was there five years. Four years later, the people said, “well I think the show should go on two-fers” you know what I mean — they had to cut the price, see it wasn’t doing so good, that’s what they told Michael.
